approach: Wire `resolve`/`run_routed` into the job run. (1) Config: optional `[ci] wait_s = 1500` section, same shape as `[disk]`. (2) `ci_result.rs` gains a small `CiBranches` trait (head, push, delete), `ci_branch(job)` and a pure `wait_for(wait_s, pause, changed)`. A new `run/ci.rs` holds the Athena methods, the production `GitBranches`, built over the existing `gh::GitRemote` and a new `Git::delete_remote_branch`, and a cfg(test) seam. The seam carries a fake `CiBranches`, a fake `CiSource` and a zero pause. This keeps the change out of gh/remote.rs, gh/mod.rs and test_support.rs. (3) `check_and_verify` pushes `athena/ci/<job id>` first, then passes the real `GhClient` CI source and the bounded `Wait` to `run_routed` in place of `NoCi`. `run_routed` returns the runs plus the `CiRecord` when the result came from CI. `Checked` carries the record, and `verification_stage` adds a `check-source` entry holding `verify::reuse_statement`. (4) `dispatch` becomes a thin wrapper that deletes the branch on every result except a `LowDisk` hold. (5) Production fix from the critic: `gh/client.rs::parse_ci_run` maps the jobs reply to per-check steps (the `fmt` job, the `clippy` job, and all `test (shard …)` jobs combined), treats gate-reused passes as success, and makes an unattributable red run fail all three checks. The jobs request asks for 100 jobs. (6) ci.yml gains the push trigger, with the header comment saying why it is allowed despite D125. (7) A workflow-file change gives a one-poll wait. Docs and CHANGELOG are updated.

decisions.choice: A small `CiBranches` trait in ci_result.rs (head, push, delete). Production impl `GitBranches` in run/ci.rs wraps `gh::GitRemote` (head and push, which exist) and `Git::delete_remote_branch` (new). The test seam is a cfg(test) thread-local in run/ci.rs carrying (Rc<dyn CiBranches>, Rc<dyn CiSource>, pause).
decisions.reason: Answers findings 1, 3 and 4. The brief's own assumption says push and delete go 'behind an injectable trait for tests', and ci_result.rs is a listed deliverable. This drops gh/remote.rs, gh/mod.rs and test_support.rs from the plan. The fake lives in the test file, not in a shared support module.

rejected.why: It touches three files outside the deliverables (remote.rs, gh/mod.rs, test_support.rs).

rejected.option: A new field on `Athena` for the injected sources
rejected.why: `Athena` is built literally in many tests and the CLI, so every site would change.

decisions.choice: Keep the off-deliverable files that cannot be avoided, each for one reason. run/ci.rs (new) holds the Athena methods and the seam, because run/mod.rs is 66 KB and the push and delete code is one concern. run/verification.rs builds the verifier's inputs and `Checked`, so the reuse statement goes there. gh/early.rs gets a one-word visibility change (`https_github_repository` becomes pub(crate)), so the https github.com gate is not copied. gh/tests.rs holds the existing `parse_ci_run` test, which asserts the old one-step format and must change. run/tests.rs only gets pub(super) on helpers. run/ci_tests.rs (new) holds the run-level tests.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 5 to 8 and 2. Each file is needed by a stated step, and none gains behavior beyond the wiring.

rejected.why: It makes a 66 KB file larger and mixes test fakes into production code.

rejected.option: Copy the https github.com check into run/ci.rs
rejected.why: Two copies of a gate that decides where Athena pushes can drift apart.

decisions.choice: Rewrite `parse_ci_run` (gh/client.rs) to read per-check conclusions from the jobs reply: job named `fmt`, job named `clippy`, and the combination of all jobs named `test (…)`. The combination is failure if any shard is failure, cancelled or timed out. Matching is on exact names, so the `ci` job named `fmt, clippy, tests` is not taken for `fmt`. A missing check job gives no step. When the gate job succeeded and the check jobs were skipped, that is a reused pass, and all three are `success`. When the run conclusion is `failure` and no step is failure, all three become `failure`. The fetch asks for `jobs?filter=latest&per_page=100`.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 9, 10 and 11. Today one step conclusion is given to all three checks, and in ci.yml that step is in the fmt job only, so a red test shard would become three passed records. The gate-skip case would leave no steps, so the commonest green run would fall back to local. `ci.yml` has more than 30 jobs, so the jobs request needs the page size. The reason then names only the failed check, which `judge` already writes as 'check <name> failed'.

rejected.option: Keep the single-step lookup and drop open question 1
rejected.why: It passes a red test shard in production.

rejected.option: Read the failing check from job logs
rejected.why: Log text is never used; the conclusions are fixed fields.

decisions.choice: Delete the CI branch in a thin `dispatch` wrapper. The current `dispatch` is renamed (for example `dispatch_run`). The wrapper calls it, then calls `drop_ci_branch`, which deletes the branch on any result except an `Err` that downcasts to `disk::LowDisk`, and only when `remote_head` shows the branch and the run is not nested. A deletion failure is a warning line.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 14. `?` errors from `produce_and_verify` or `resume_candidate` skip `close_dispatched`, so a delete placed there leaks the branch. A `LowDisk` hold is the one case where the job stays dispatched and resumes, so its branch must stay. A crash before the wrapper returns still leaks, and ci-routing.md says so.

rejected.why: Error exits leave the branch behind, against 'whatever the outcome'.
It would also delete on a disk hold.

decisions.choice: Push at the top of `check_and_verify` when `recorded_checks` is None, skipping nested runs and any origin that is not an https github.com URL. A push failure is a warning, and that run then uses `NoCi` with one poll (local checks).
decisions.reason: This is the first step after admission and also covers a resume. Pushing the same SHA twice is a git no-op. It covers criterion 4 (no remote or no GitHub changes nothing).

rejected.why: A resumed job would never push.

decisions.choice: `ci_result::wait_for(wait_s, pause, changed)` returns polls = ceil(wait_s / pause) normally, and one poll when a changed path starts with `WORKFLOW_DIR`. The wiring calls it, so the SHA rules in `resolve` are untouched.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 13. A workflow change makes `resolve` distrust a green run, so waiting up to 25 minutes is wasted time on top of the local run.

rejected.why: The brief puts the SHA rules out of scope.

decisions.choice: `run_routed` returns `RoutedRuns { runs, ci: Option<CiRecord> }`. `ci` is Some only for a CI-sourced Verified or Failed. The verifier's `check-source` entry (not a check, passed = true) uses `verify::reuse_statement(&record, &candidate)`, and only when the source is CI. verify.rs and the `CiSource` impl on `GhClient` are otherwise unchanged.
decisions.reason: The statement needs the record's SHA, run address and steps, which only `run_routed` holds. It follows the existing `producer-report-gaps` entry, so no brief change is needed. `reuse_statement` returns None for a SHA mismatch.

rejected.option: Rebuild the record from check notes
rejected.why: It parses free text and loses the run address and duration.
It touches the context crate's briefs and token-budget tests.

decisions.choice: `wait_s` goes in a new optional `[ci]` section (`CiConfig`), default 1500, reset in `reading_inputs` the way `disk` is. The poll pause is a fixed 20 s constant (`CI_POLL_PAUSE`).
decisions.reason: `Budget` has no per-field defaults, so a new field there would break every config literal. The reset keeps readings' config digest unchanged.

rejected.why: It breaks every config literal and fixture.

decisions.choice: ci.yml: `push: branches: [main, 'athena/ci/**']`. The header comment says the second push run is allowed on purpose. D125 removed push runs for PR branches because the two runs of one commit each ran the full 16 minutes. Athena pushes this branch to get a run for the exact SHA to read, and `early_pr` opens a pull request for the same SHA, which gives a second `ci` run. `GhClient::fetch` takes the newest `ci` run by `created_at` for the SHA, so either run serves. ci-routing.md says the same.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 12. The request asks for the trigger. The duplicate cost is stated, not hidden.

rejected.why: It is outside this request and changes landing.

risks.risk: The wait blocks `check_and_verify` for up to 25 minutes while holding the job lock and a check slot.
risks.mitigation: The bound is in athena.toml. A missing, cancelled, timed-out or unreachable result falls back to local at once, a fetch error returns Missing without more waiting, and a workflow-file change gives one poll. Tests use a zero pause, so none sleeps.

risks.risk: A red run caused by a non-check job in ci.yml (history, attribution) with fmt, clippy and test all green fails all three checks and rejects the job.
risks.mitigation: This fails closed, as the critic asked. The reason names the three checks. The case is listed in open questions for the maintainer to rule on.

risks.risk: Job names in ci.yml change (for example `fmt` renamed), so the parser finds no step and the run is treated as incomplete.
risks.mitigation: A missing step gives no step, `resolve` does not trust a green run that lacks one, and the job falls back to local. A red run with no attributable failure fails all three. The fixtures are built from the names in ci.yml.

risks.risk: The delete wrapper runs git against the network on every job end.
risks.mitigation: It does nothing for a nested run, a non-https-github origin, or a job whose branch is absent (`head` is None). Any failure is a warning line and never changes the outcome.

risks.risk: A crash before the wrapper returns leaks `athena/ci/<id>`.
risks.mitigation: A later close of the same job deletes it, because the delete checks `head`. The remaining window is recorded in ci-routing.md. A sweep is out of scope.

risks.risk: Existing run tests with an https github origin would reach the real `gh` through the push.
risks.mitigation: In cfg(test) builds, `push_ci_branch` and `drop_ci_branch` do nothing unless the seam is installed, and only the new tests install it.

risks.risk: A new `[ci]` section changes the config digest of readings or trips the admission rule for config changes.
risks.mitigation: The field is Option, skipped when absent, and reset in `reading_inputs` as `disk` is. A test asserts the digest is unchanged.

risks.risk: Pushing the candidate sends its content to the remote.
risks.mitigation: The candidate has already passed admission, and `early_pr` already pushes the same commit. The branch is deleted at close.

demonstrations.method: Run-level test through the real job run. The test capability has fmt, clippy and test checks whose command is `false`, so any local run fails the job. The fake CI source returns a finished `success` run for the exact candidate SHA with three passed steps. A routing-level test counts `Exec` calls.
demonstrations.observes: The job ends Landed. The fake `Exec` was called 0 times and all three check records carry the note 'result reused from the CI run <address> for <sha>'. The fake source was asked for the SHA that the finished job's record names as its candidate. The routing-level test asserts `Exec` count 0 and `RoutedRuns.ci.source == Source::Ci`.
demonstrations.fails_without: With `NoCi` still passed, the source is never read, the `false` commands run, the checks fail and the job is Rejected. With the exact-SHA rule dropped, the stale-SHA test in criterion 2 fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `Athena::go` (run/mod.rs), which reaches `dispatch`, `check_and_verify`, `push_ci_branch`, `routing::run_routed` and `ci_result::resolve`. Guards: origin is an https github.com URL, the run is not nested, and the capability lists fmt, clippy and test. The fixture is `ci::seam::install(branches, source, pause)`, a cfg(test) thread-local added by plan step 4 in run/ci.rs. It carries a `CiFake` (implements `CiBranches` and `CiSource`) defined in run/ci_tests.rs. Agents come from the existing `FakeAgentDriver` script in run/tests.rs (exists). The test repository gets origin `https://github.com/example/project.git` the way `early_run` in run_pin_tests.rs does (exists). The test capability is added by step 8.

demonstrations.method: Run-level tests, one per case, with the same fixtures. (a) Red: the fake returns a `failure` run whose parsed steps are fmt success, clippy success, test failure. The job is Rejected with reason 'check test failed', not 'check fmt failed', and `Exec` is never called. (b) A green run for another SHA: the local checks run (commands `true`), the notes do not name CI, and the job Lands. (c) Missing (None), cancelled, timed_out and skipped runs, and a run that stays unfinished through the bound: each falls back to the local checks. Production-parser tests: `parse_ci_run` on recorded jobs-reply fixtures in gh/tests.rs. (i) fmt and clippy job success with one `test (shard 3)` failure gives fmt and clippy success and test failure. (ii) An all-green run gives three success steps. (iii) A gate that succeeded with fmt, clippy and the test shards skipped gives three success steps. (iv) A failed gate with skipped checks gives three failure steps. (v) The `fmt, clippy, tests` job is not taken for `fmt`. A routing test feeds the (i) fixture through `run_routed` with a counting `Exec`: fmt and clippy pass, test fails, and `Exec` is called 0 times.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-core ci_checks_red ci_checks_other_sha ci_checks_missing ci_checks_cancelled ci_checks_timed_out ci_checks_unfinished parse_ci_run routing_
demonstrations.observes: Red: the state is Rejected, the reason contains 'check test failed' and not 'check fmt failed', and the `false` commands were never run. Other SHA, missing, cancelled, timed out and unfinished: the job Lands through the local checks, with 3 local `Exec` calls in the routing tests. The parser fixtures give exactly the per-check conclusions listed above.
demonstrations.fails_without: If red mapped to fallback, the `true` commands would pass and the job would Land, but the test expects Rejected. If a stale SHA were accepted, the `false` commands would never run and the job would pass. With the old single-step parser, fixture (i) would give test success, and fixture (iii) would give no steps and a local fallback.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: `Athena::go`, `routing::run_routed` and `gh::parse_ci_run` (all exist). The run-level fixture is `ci::seam::install` with `CiFake` configured with a `Result<Option<CiRun>>` (step 4). The parser fixtures are JSON values built with `json!` in gh/tests.rs (the existing style; exists). The routing tests reuse the `Ci` and `Local` fakes in routing.rs (exist), and the `go` helper there is updated for `RoutedRuns` (step 3).

demonstrations.method: Run-level test with `CiFake` recording every `push`, `delete` and `head` call with a probe that reads the `FakeAgentDriver`'s invocation count. Three outcomes: accepted (green CI), rejected (red CI), and failed (the agent script makes the producer fail). A disk-hold variant checks that the branch stays when the result is a `LowDisk` error.
demonstrations.observes: Exactly one push of `athena/ci/<job id>` at the candidate commit, recorded after the producer's invocation and before the verifier's. Exactly one delete of the same branch, recorded after the job closed with Landed, Rejected or Failed. In the disk-hold variant there is no delete and the branch is still present in the fake. The push-failure variant gives one warning line and a local run.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the push missing, the push assertion fails and the fake source is read for an SHA never pushed. With the delete missing on the rejected or failed path, the delete count stays 0. With the delete done on a `LowDisk` hold, the hold variant fails.

open_questions: A red `ci` run caused only by a non-check job (history or attribution) now fails fmt, clippy and test together. Should the parser instead ignore jobs that are not required checks?
A job whose process dies before the `dispatch` wrapper returns leaves its `athena/ci/<id>` branch until a later close of the same job. A periodic sweep is out of scope.
The per-check duration is 0 for CI steps, as before; the run's total time is kept. Job `started_at`/`completed_at` could fill it in a later job.
Does the fake agent script in run/tests.rs let a producer write a path under `.github/workflows/`? If it does not, the workflow-change one-poll rule is shown by the `wait_for` unit test alone.
